#Mounts

A mount is a folder of one machine, seen on another: ~/Pictures of the laptop at /mnt/photos on vps1, read-only, or serviceman's own data/ at /mnt/serviceman. The machine it is mounted on reads it, and writes it too when the mount is read-write, as any folder of its own; the files stay where they are.

The page is Mounts, on All categories beside Shared folders. + Mount… picks the machine the folder is on and the folder, the machine it is mounted on and where, and the mode: read-only or read-write. Each mount is a row: where it stands, what is wrong with it, what went through it. A row's actions (a click on a row opens them where the table has no room) set it aside and back without retyping it, edit it, or forget it, which takes it out of the config and unmounts it.

#How it works

No ssh and no key: the machines' agents are already there, and a mount goes from one to the other as a forward does (Remotes).

  1. serviceman tells the machine at to its mounts, at its hello, after the config changes and on the minute.
  2. Its agent listens on a socket file of its own for each one, 0600, in its folder's mounts/, and hands the table to its root half.
  3. The root half mounts each with sshfs. In place of ssh, sshfs runs the agent's own file, --pipe <the socket>, which joins sshfs to that socket.
  4. The agent takes what comes in on the socket straight to the agent of the machine at from, over the tailnet, on its peer port, asked with the token serviceman gave that machine; that agent serves the folder over SFTP. serviceman tells the one where the other listens, and the other which mounts it may be asked for, and carries none of the bytes.
  5. Through serviceman when it has to: a folder of serviceman's own state dir, an agent from before the straight way at either end, or a peer that does not answer within 3 seconds (asked again 30 seconds later). The agent then carries it over its link, as a stream named for the mount, and serviceman joins it to the folder: a stream over the link of the machine at from, or its own server for its state dir. The row says which way it goes, and why when it is not straight.

When a link blinks, sshfs dials its pipe again by itself (reconnect). A restart of either agent leaves the mount where it is: sshfs runs on its own, and the socket is there again at the agent's next hello.

#What the far machine sees

The folder, and nothing else. / over there is the folder here, and .. stops at it. A link inside the folder that leads out of it is not followed: not by a path that goes through it, not by an open file, which is checked again once it is open. A link is never made over a mount: one made here could lead a program of this machine out of the folder. Neither is an owner changed. What it is told when something fails is the kind of failure, never a path of this machine.

A read-only mount is read-only twice: the folder's server refuses every change, and sshfs mounts it with ro. root on the machine it is mounted on reads every file the mount shows, as it reads its own disk: a folder with keys in it, serviceman's data/ above all, gives them to that machine's root. Mount the part that is needed (logs, not .) when that is enough.

#What a row says

State What it means
mounted It is there, as the row says
starting Told to the machine, not answered yet
set aside Written down, not mounted
vps1 offline The machine it is mounted on is away; it is mounted once its agent dials in
agent too old An agent at either end is older than mounts; update it
in use A changed mode waits for the processes that hold the path; the row names them
not empty The path holds files of its own, which the mount would hide; nothing is moved
path taken Another file system is mounted there
cannot mount The machine has no root half (sudo bin/install-root in the agent's folder)
failed sshfs said why, or sshfs is not there and apt could not install it; tried again every minute

A mounted row whose folder's machine is away says so: the folder answers nothing until it is back.

#What it needs

  • The agent, 1.38 or newer, on both machines; on to only, for a folder of serviceman's own.
  • The agent's root half on to, which mounts over any folder of that machine. sshfs is installed with apt when it is missing.
  • A path at to that is empty or not there yet, one level below the top at least (/mnt/photos), and none of the system's own folders.

#What it cannot do

  • A machine away is a folder that answers nothing. The files are on the other machine.
  • Two agents that cannot reach each other go through serviceman. Then a mount between two VPSes is as fast as their links to serviceman, not as the link between them; the row says so, and why.
  • A database does not go in it. SQLite and its like want a local disk.

#For the operator

Where What
mounts in serviceman.json The mounts (Config)
<the agent's folder>/mounts/*.sock The sockets sshfs dials, the agent's user's alone; in the temp folder's serviceman-mounts-<uid>/ when that path is too long for a socket file
/var/lib/serviceman/mounts/table.json The root half's table: what it mounts, and what each try said; root's

The log lines are mounts_* and mount_error on serviceman, mount_socket_* and root_mounts_keep_* on a machine (The log).
